title: Jordan decomposition as a chain of similarity transitivity steps
intent: Prove the main theorem of the file — that a square matrix A over a closed field is similar to its Jordan form — by chaining four similarity lemmas through `similar_trans`: A to its Frobenius form (`Frobenius`), that to its closed-field block form (`similar_Frobenius`), then blockwise to `Jordan_form A` (`similar_diag_block`), each companion block becoming a Jordan block per root (`similar_cj`).

parent.name: Jordan
parent.statement: Lemma Jordan n (A : 'M[R]_n.+1) : similar A (Jordan_form A).

Lemma Frobenius n (A : 'M[F]_n.+1) :
  similar A (Frobenius_form A).
children.closed_by: applies `similar_fundamental`, then chains char-poly equivalences with `equiv_trans` (`equiv_Smith`, `equiv_Frobenius_seq`, `equiv_sbc_ssc`, `equiv_diag_block`, `Smith_companion`), closing with `exact: monic_invariant_factors` (line 399)

children.name: similar_Frobenius
children.statement:
Lemma similar_Frobenius n (A : 'M[R]_n.+1) :
 similar (Frobenius_form A) (Frobenius_form_CF A).
children.closed_by: unfolds both form definitions, then induction over `invariant_factors A` re-factors each block using `similar_poly_inv`, `similar_drblockmx`, `similar_ulblockmx`, `similar_cast`; the empty and singleton base cases close with `exact: similar_refl` (lines 684, 714, 721)

children.name: similar_diag_block
children.statement:
Lemma similar_diag_block : forall l1 l2, size l1 = size l2 ->
   forall (F1 F2 : forall n : nat, nat -> 'M[R]_n.+1),
   (forall i, i < size l1 ->
    similar (F1 (nth 0%N l1 i) i) (F2 (nth 0%N l2 i) i)) ->
   similar (diag_block_mx l1 F1) (diag_block_mx l2 F2).
children.closed_by: double induction over the two block-size lists with `seq2_ind`, joining the head blocks by `similar_dgblockmx` and the tails by the induction hypothesis; the empty case closes with `similar_refl` (line 303)

children.name: similar_cj
children.statement:
Lemma similar_cj n (lam : R) :
  similar (companion_mx (('X - lam%:P)^+ n.+1)) (Jordan_block lam n.+1).
children.closed_by: proves the companion matrix of ('X - lam%:P)^+ n.+1 is similar to Jordan_block lam n.+1 by `similar_fundamental` then a chain of Smith-normal-form equivalences (`equiv_Smith`, `Smith_companion`, `Smith_gcdr_spec`), identifying the char poly with `char_poly_Jordan_block` (line 142); the gcd computation closes with `apply/dvdrP; exists ((-1)^+ n); rewrite -expr2 sqrr_sign` (line 167)

applicability.goal_shape: A similarity goal `similar A B` where `similar` is the mathcomp-compatible similarity relation, `A` is an `'M[R]_n.+1` matrix over a `closedFieldType`, and `B` is a canonical block form (`Jordan_form A`); the proof is a right-nested chain of `similar_trans` steps through intermediate canonical forms.
applicability.use_when: an end-to-end normalisation splits into stages that each already have a named similarity lemma (over the base field, then over the algebraic closure, then blockwise); the stages compose with `similar_trans`, and a generic blockwise lemma (`similar_diag_block`) plus one per-block lemma (`similar_cj`) exist.
applicability.avoid_when: a stage has no standalone lemma yet (the chain forces one lemma per stage before the glue can be written); the intermediate forms differ in dimension or base field so `similar_trans` cannot bridge them; the per-block step needs a different argument per block rather than one uniform lemma.

consequences: Turns one large similarity-to-canonical-form goal into one transitivity chain of four named lemmas, so each hole is one stage of the normalisation — the natural unit for a bounded prover. Obligations: each child must be a full `similar` statement with matching dimensions; the glue's application order must match the chain of intermediate forms; the intermediate forms (`Frobenius_form A`, `Frobenius_form_CF A`) must be spelled out so consecutive `similar_trans` instances typecheck; the blockwise step needs the block-size lists to have equal size (proved in the glue at lines 212-214). Failure mode: the glue does no real work itself, so a missing or misshaped stage lemma surfaces as a type error at the `similar_trans` application rather than as a subgoal to prove.
